label: Equine passports and identification documents
description: UK legal controls specifically governing equine passports, horse passports, equine identification documents, and the statutory identification of equidae/equids. Covers issuing, holding, updating, replacing, returning, surrendering, invalidating and producing equine passports or identification documents where those duties are expressly tied to horses, ponies, donkeys, mules or other equidae. Includes equine microchipping/transponders, unique equine lifetime numbers (UELN), passport issuing organisations, central equine databases, equine registers, keeper/owner duties connected to passport records, food-chain status declarations recorded in equine passports, veterinary medicine records recorded in equine passports, imported equines where passport or identification-document duties apply, and enforcement of equine identification duties. Do not treat generic references to animals, horses, owners, keepers, registers, databases, movement, imports, slaughter, medicine, passports, or electronic identification as sufficient unless the source is clearly about equine passports, horse passports, equine identification, identification of equidae, UELNs, equine microchips/transponders, passport issuing organisations, central equine databases, or equine registers.
synonyms: methods for the identification of equidae
exclusions: pet passports for dogs, cats or ferrets only
animal health certificates for pets only
racehorse ownership or gambling regulation only
breed society rules only without statutory passport or identification obligations
tourism or riding school licensing only
general animal welfare only without equine identification or passport duties
veterinary medicines generally without equine passport food-chain status or medicine-record duties
livestock identification for cattle, sheep, goats, pigs or poultry only
vehicle or transport documentation unrelated to equine identification
immigration or border passports for people

metadata.conversion_note: Ada category brief tightened after an initial discovery run over-matched broad standalone terms. Synonyms now contain only anchored compound terms suitable for standalone Lex queries; broad species and generic administrative terms are retained only as weak/supporting triage signals.

likely_accept: UK, Great Britain, England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland instruments directly regulating equine passports, horse passports, equine identification documents, identification of equidae/equines, UELNs, equine microchipping/transponders, passport issuing organisations, central equine databases, equine registers, replacement/surrender/invalidation of equine passports, or enforcement of equine identification duties.
Assimilated EU or EU-derived instruments that form part of the UK legal framework for identification of equidae or equine passport requirements.
Instruments specifically amending, revoking, preserving, commencing, transitioning, or enforcing a core equine passport or equine identification instrument.
needs_human_review: Import, movement, disease-control or animal health instruments that expressly refer to equine passports or equine identification documents but may not be the main source of passport duties.
Revoked or historical equine passport/identification instruments that may be predecessors of the current regime.
Northern Ireland or EU-derived material where post-Brexit applicability may require legal review.
Guidance, explanatory memoranda, official forms, database material, or operational documents that help interpret or apply equine passport rules.
park_contextual: General animal health, veterinary medicines, slaughter, food-chain, import, movement, or traceability material that mentions equines or horses but is not primarily about equine passports or statutory equine identification.
Breed society, stud book, competition, racing, welfare, transport, or riding establishment material that may interact with passport rules but is not itself a legal source for passport obligations.
Pet travel or animal health certificate material where equines are mentioned only incidentally.
likely_reject: Human passport, immigration, nationality, border document, or travel document material.
Electronic identification or trust-services instruments for people, companies, digital transactions, or online identity systems unless expressly about equine identification.
Pet passport material for dogs, cats, or ferrets unless it expressly also regulates equine passports.
Horse racing betting, race-horse duty, gambling, racecourse, prize, or sporting rules with no statutory equine identification duties.

Generic animal welfare, transport, veterinary, import, disease-control, tax, mining, local-improvement, education, or administrative instruments with no clear equine passport, equine identification, microchip, UELN, register, or database connection.
Livestock identification material for cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry, camelids, deer, bees, fish, or other species only.

References to horses, ponies, donkeys, mules, zebras or other animals in local Acts, workplace/mining Acts, cruelty Acts, tax Acts or transport Acts where there is no passport/identification-document duty.
triage_guidance.triage_rule: Weak terms are supporting signals only and must not make a candidate likely_accept or high confidence on their own. A likely_accept source should contain an anchor such as equine passport, horse passport, equine identification, identification of equidae/equines, UELN, equine microchip/transponder, passport issuing organisation, central equine database, or equine register. Broad species words such as horse, pony, donkey, mule, zebra, equine, equid or equidae are not sufficient unless combined with passport, identification, microchip, transponder, UELN, register, database, issuing organisation/body, or an amendment/revocation/transitional provision clearly tied to a core equine identification/passport source.
